Prerequisites: Linear algebra, multivariable calculus, and basic probability
CourseOutcomes: CO1: Understand core machine learning paradigms, inductive bias, and hypothesis spaces
CO2: Implement and analyze regression, classification, neural networks, and backpropagation
CO3: Formulate optimization algorithms, loss functions, and regularization techniques for generalization
CO4: Design clustering and dimensionality reduction models for unsupervised data analysis
CO5: Deploy machine learning pipelines for electrical engineering power systems, forecasting, and fault diagnosis
Textbooks: Tom M. Mitchell, Machine Learning, McGraw Hill International Edition, 2017.
Christopher M. Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, Springer, 2009.
Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, Aaron Courville, Deep Learning, MIT Press, 2016.
